Content: Extended council-style repository audit campaign on audit/skeleton-animation-improvements-2026-09-07. Reviewed the repo council skill and used independent simulated seats because no independently invokable /council subagent was exposed. More than 390 explicitly numbered rounds plus additional distinct micro-rounds were performed across runtime generation, editor workflow, serialization, validation/sequencing, skeleton/IK, API ownership, resource lifetime, concurrency, numeric policy, compatibility/migration, performance, determinism, and adversarial equivalence. The campaign intentionally suppressed stale findings and duplicate task creation. Confirmed/fixed: generated-output collection and nested influence ownership, material-region input ownership, GeneratedCreatureData color ownership, clone-policy consolidation, one-resolution radius bridge, AppearanceBaker null contracts, MaterialRegion integer-overflow validation, SDF temp-buffer exception disposal, non-repairing CapsuleAxis canonicalization, NormalizeOr invalid-fallback contract, skeleton queue simplification, and preview component ownership hardening. Confirmed/tracked: TSK-0156 mutable Bone/Skeleton model; TSK-0159 mutable CreaturePart elements retained by hierarchy index; TSK-0154 broader GeneratedCreatureData ownership across async publication; TSK-0160 malformed MeshExtractionResult operations; TSK-0162 source fix awaiting validation; TSK-0163 BodyFrame default handedness mismatch; TSK-0164 JSON writer control-character escaping mismatch; TSK-0165 Unity-native Gradient/AnimationCurve evaluation from background Task.Run; TSK-0056 post-quantization key collisions; TSK-0095 snapshot/stage ownership umbrella. A subsequent branch-state review found duplicate task keys in the imported task directory: TSK-0166, TSK-0167, and TSK-0168 each had multiple independent records. The duplicate records were safely renumbered as TSK-0170 through TSK-0173 while preserving the earlier stable keys, and TSK-0169 references were updated to the renumbered TSK-0172 skinning-smear investigation. TSK-0169's editor skinning sweep implementation is now tracked as InProgress pending Unity validation. A fresh low-level skinning pass found that LinearBlendSkinning validated influence count, index range, finiteness, and weights but accepted duplicate BoneIndex entries within a vertex. This was hardened under TSK-0174 with a focused regression. The first implementation used HashSet per vertex; adversarial performance review caught that allocation in the mesh deformation hot path and it was immediately replaced with a bounded O(16) nested comparison because the influence cap is four. Preserve the full source contract documentation when making future surgical edits. Continue treating task id/key uniqueness as a hard invariant and hot-path allocation behavior as a first-class correctness/performance concern. Do not blanket-convert Unity authoring palette Entries to immutable APIs. No Unity execution was performed; no new test is claimed as passing in Unity. Branch remains the working feature branch.
Conflicts: Older audits may still describe backing-list leaks, duplicate resolution paths, shallow GeneratedCreatureData colors, or the old canonicalizer CapsuleAxis repair; those findings are stale where current source now fixes them.

The repository task-tracker skill calls for MemorySmith MCP actions; that connector was unavailable here, so repository JSON was used as the existing fallback and remains subject to later MemorySmith reconciliation.

Task IDs must remain unique even when multiple agents/audit passes create closely related records; preserve the earliest stable key and renumber later independent records rather than silently keeping duplicate keys.

Unity validation remains a separate evidence tier. Source inspection and focused tests can establish source-level confidence, but generated-creature deformation, editor reload behavior, and SkinnedMeshRenderer parity remain Unity-gated until actually exercised.
